500px provided description: Har Ki Pauri, Haridwar - The Holy City of India ?Thakur Dalip Singh

Har Ki Pauri is a famous ghat on the banks of the river Ganges in Haridwar in Uttarakhand state in India. This revered place is the major landmark of the holy city of Haridwar. It is believed that it is precise spot where the Ganges leaves the mountains and enters the plains. The ghat is on the west bank of Ganges canal through which the Ganges is diverted just to the north. Har Ki Pauri is also the area where thousands of pilgrims converge and the festivities commence like the Kumbha Mela and Vaisakhi.

An area within Har Ki Pauri, is considered most sacred Place in India. Every day, Har Ki Pauri ghat witnesses hundreds taking a dip in water of the Ganges. The place is considered very auspicious. Over the years the ghats have undergone major extension and renovation as the crowds increased in subsequent Kumbh Melas. Jai Ganga Maa Har Ki Pauri (Hindi: हर की पौड़ी) is a famous ghat on the banks of the Ganges in Haridwar in the Indian state of Uttarakhand. This revered place is the major landmark of the holy city of Haridwar. Literally, "Har" means "Lord Shiva" who is the god according to shaivite Rishav Bhagwan school of Hindu theology, "Ki" means "of" and "Pauri" means "steps". Lord Shiva and Lord Vishnu are believed to have visited the Brahmakund in Har Ki Pauri in the Vedic times. There is a large footprint said to belong to Lord Vishnu on a stone wall.[1]
It is believed that it is precise spot where the Ganges leaves the mountains and enters the plains. The ghat is on the west bank of Ganges canal through which the Ganges is diverted just to the north. Har Ki Pauri is also the area where thousands of pilgrims converge and the festivities commence during the Kumbha Mela, which takes place every twelve years, and the Ardh Kumbh Mela, which takes place every six years and the Punjabi festival of Vaisakhi, a harvest festival occurring every year in the month of April .

ImageDescription.value:
In the northern Indian state of Uttarakhand, where the Ganges River emerges from the Himalayan foothills, lies the historic city of Haridwar, a significant Hindu pilgrimage location. A gateway to the four revered Char Dham pilgrimage sites of Gangotri, Yamunotri, Kedarnath, and Badrinath, it is one of the seven holiest destinations for Hindus.

The nightly Ganga Aarti ritual is held in the Har Ki Pauri ghat, one of the numerous temples in Haridwar that are well-known for their religious significance. Priests offer prayers and float lamps on the river during the exquisite and poignant Ganga Aarti rite.

Retreats for yoga and meditation are also common in Haridwar. Haridwar is home to several ashrams and yoga studios, and many visitors travel here to advance their spiritual practises.

Haridwar is a lovely city with a lot to offer visitors in addition to its religious importance. The Ganges River flows through the heart of the city, which is flanked by forested hills and hills of lush greenery. Along with a plethora of historical and cultural landmarks, Haridwar also has a large number of parks and gardens.

You may engage in the following activities in Haridwar:

Visit the Ganga Aarti ritual in the Har Ki Pauri ghat. Swim in the revered Ganges River. Visit the Chandi Devi Temple and Mansa Devi Temple, two temples perched on hillsides that offer breathtaking views of the Ganges River and the city. Check out the Bharat Mata shrine, a special shrine honouring Mother India. Visit the Rishikesh-Haridwar Ropeway for breathtaking views of the hills around the Ganges River. Visit the wildlife refuge at the Rajaji National Park, which is close to Haridwar. Visit the Kumbh Mela Museum to learn about the history of the greatest religious gathering on earth, the Kumbh Mela.

Haridwar is a genuinely unique location that anyone with an interest should explore.

Allahabad - Prayagraj, Uttar Pradesh, the Ganges. My second day in Prayagraj: walking in the morning, by boat in the evening.

Kumbh Mela is a mass Hindu pilgrimage of faith in which Hindus gather to bathe in a sacred or holy river. The festival site is located on the banks of the river: the confluence (Sangam) of the Ganges and the Yamuna and the invisible Sarasvati at Allahabad. Bathing in this river is thought to cleanse a person of all their sins.
